solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Professional baritone upset one being tried out

parts.note: pro is short for a professional

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of baritone are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A paid singer whose performance has been disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professional' looks like it describes the singer, but it supplies its short form; 'upset' scrambles only the singer's voice type into BATIONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A probationer is a newcomer serving a trial period before being confirmed in a job.

clue.text: A change of insides — ref is on top of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on top of something means coming before it in the word

parts.note: taken as written, short for referee
taken as written

explanation.surface: A referee perched on top of something that is being overhauled inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on top of' works only because this is a down answer, where the upper piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit renews the internal fittings of something, such as a ship, so its insides are changed.

clue.text: Who works on toes held by footballer in agony

indicators.note: held by says the answer is gripped within the run of words footballer in agony

explanation.surface: An injured footballer writhing in pain, perhaps over a stamped-on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in classical ballet performs on the tips of her toes, en pointe.

clue.text: Subject to go for mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to go for something is to pick it

explanation.surface: A matter one is inclined to choose most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of PICK, leaving PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion or study is a theme, the matter being talked about.

clue.text: Caedmon's central character in Old English verse

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the abbreviation
the central character of a word is its middle letter, here taken from Caedmon

explanation.surface: Caedmon, the earliest named English poet, wrote a hymn in Old English verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' takes D, the middle of CAEDMON, set inside OE. Caedmon was a 7th-century Anglo-Saxon poet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so it is a piece of verse.

clue.text: Clear I'd got wrapped up in incident

indicators.note: being wrapped up in something means being enclosed by it

parts.note: an incident is an event, something that happens
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits plainly that they became absorbed in an incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got wrapped up in' reads as being engrossed, but it signals enclosure; the apostrophe of I'd is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, obvious, just as a clear fact is.

clue.text: Take another look at American's 100% overpayment

definitions.meaning: paying twice is a double cheque, spelt check in the US

explanation.surface: Reviewing a bill to find that an American paid twice as much as owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: paying a bill twice is a 100% overpayment, and an American writes cheque as check.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify something a second time is to inspect it once more for errors.

clue.text: Hasty and careless entry for cup goes adrift

indicators.note: drifting off course means the letters of entry for cup wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A team's application for a cup competition gets lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfunctory effort is done quickly as a routine duty, with little care or interest.

clue.text: Meat for haggis, perhaps no longer fresh — a pound

parts.note: food that has gone off is no longer fresh
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shopper complains that haggis meat has turned, at a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is a Scottish dish of sheep's heart, liver and lungs, hence the 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible internal organs of an animal, the classic filling of a haggis.

clue.text: Officiate live, following pressure

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the pressure symbol

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a live event while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts RESIDE after P. 'live' is read as the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair a meeting or ceremony, conducting it as the one in charge.

clue.text: Flower spread gets trophy

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread
a cup is a trophy awarded to winners

explanation.surface: A flower show contest where the winning bloom spreads and takes a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of meadows.

clue.text: Important for pit not to be empty

parts.note: being for something is being pro it
a pit is a mine

indicators.note: an empty word loses its contents, keeping only the outer letters of not

explanation.surface: A miner insists the colliery must not be left abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be empty' keeps NT, the outside letters of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent person or thing stands out as notable and significant.

clue.text: Fantastic being regularly well-off

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth of well-off

explanation.surface: A wealthy person whose good fortune seems almost unreal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a creature of fantasy and folklore, a mythical small being.

clue.text: Require time during unusual dissection of alien

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the other
an unusual cutting-up of alien rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A laboratory needs time to carry out a strange autopsy on an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual dissection of' makes ENAIL from ALIEN; 'during' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as a necessary consequence, so it means to necessitate.

clue.text: Twisting in roots is unusual

indicators.note: being unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of in roots are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree whose roots grow in a contorted way is a rare sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, or the strain produced by it.

clue.text: Bad to rent — bad

indicators.note: the second bad signals that the letters of to rent go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renting is a bad idea, says someone, repeating themselves for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Bad' is the definition; the second is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten describes something decayed or of very poor quality.

clue.text: The woman Basil cut short?

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: basil is a herb

explanation.surface: A woman who interrupted a man named Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name, but it is the herb; 'cut short' removes the final B of HERB.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to a female person in object position, as in 'I saw the woman'.

clue.text: Avoiding alcohol, having gone without can

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: someone who has gone is absent
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone who has gone without a can of beer is staying dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from indulgence, especially from drinking.

clue.text: Sons press for big increase

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A father's sons push hard for a substantial rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful rise, as in demand or voltage.

clue.text: What's in tea tent — to be this?

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about the fate of the food laid out in a tea tent at a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Food in a tea tent is meant to be consumed, so its destiny is to be devoured.

clue.text: Note lithe mountaineer

parts.note: C is a musical note
lithe means supple, limber

explanation.surface: A message about an agile mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message but is the musical note C.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer scales peaks, so is one who ascends rock faces.

clue.text: Friend in the US, one not yet out

definitions.meaning: American slang for a pal, short for buddy
a flower or leaf before it has opened

explanation.surface: An American pal who has not yet come out of hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a mate buddy for short; a plant's unopened shoot has not yet blossomed.

clue.text: Get into American's heart, not cold

indicators.note: not says the cold abbreviation is removed from the word

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre, spelt center in the US
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A plea to win over an American's heart while staying warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C from CENTER, the American spelling of centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go inside it.

clue.text: Popular commercial with gent missing good chance?

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a commercial is an advert

indicators.note: missing says the abbreviation is taken out of gent

explanation.surface: A popular advert featuring a man who misses a good opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes G from GENT, leaving ENT. 'chance' is the adjective, as in a chance meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by accident, without intention, happens by chance, unplanned.
